text:
alex: FYI saw a burst of gitlab CI runs this morning that all tried to terraform apply the gpu-batch stack in us-west-2 at the same time. one run ended up holding a consul backend lock and the others failed with lock conflicts.
maria: ouch. did any of the applies succeed partially?
alex: looks like one apply did partial state moves. they were running a state mv to split per-region workspaces, then the runner lost net and never finished. consul shows the lock key still present: `/locks/terraform/gpu-batch/2026-06-14/lock-7f3a`.
sam: can you paste the runner logs for the failing job? also which pipeline triggered the state move?
alex: pasted minimal logs from gitlab job: ```ERROR: Error acquiring lock: consul: key already locked by session 31d9aa4e```
alex: pipeline was an automated PR merge that runs `terragrunt plan && terragrunt apply --auto-approve` in the top-level infra repo. there was also an argo sync that applied a nested helm chart which caused a spike in new node requests around the same time.
maria: so two systems tried to make infra changes concurrently (gitlab CI + argo sync). the problematic job did a `terraform state mv` while holding the consul lock and then timed out. that left some GPU node ASGs referenced in the old key and not in the new key. billing spike reported by finance for us-west-2 GPUs.
ops-oncall: estimate of cost impact? finance flagged ~18 hours of extra nodes, ~$4.2k. ops already scaling down ASGs but we need to fix state.
sam: steps I'd take: 1) avoid force-unlocking without verifying; 2) check the runner that lost network — if it still exists, try to reattach or get the session id; 3) replicate state locally to inspect drift.
maria: agree. I attempted a read-only state list: ```terraform state list -state=consul://us-west-2/gpu-batch``` returned mix of old and new resources (asg.gpu_pool_old, aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_pool_v2).
alex: I also ran `consul kv get -recurse /locks/terraform/gpu-batch` and saw session 31d9aa4e active but not owned by any known runner (it was from a short-lived runner that timed out). consul shows SessionInfo: "Node: runner-98, Behavior: release, TTL: 0s" — looks orphaned.
ops-oncall: recommended safe recovery: stop autoscaler activity (pause fleet-autoscaler) to prevent further node churn, snapshot current state, then coordinate a manual unlock and finish the state move under supervision.
sam: I'm going to create a temporary readonly copy of the state locally: ```terraform state pull > state-snapshot-1862349999.tfstate``` then inspect `jq` diffs between resources. after that we can plan a controlled `terraform state mv` for the orphaned resources.
maria: before force-unlock, we should use consul API to check sessions: ```curl -sS http://consul.service.internal/v1/session/info/31d9aa4e``` - if session has no TTL renewal and Node is offline we can force-unlock.
alex: I escalated to infra-bot to open an incident and paused the GitLab project webhooks to prevent more concurrent applies. infra-bot: ``incident created: INC-2026-2793 - terraform-consul-lock-orphan-usw2``
infra-bot: reminder — do not run `terraform apply` except from the coordination channel.
ops-oncall: I'm going to run a controlled unlock in 10m if no objections, then manually run the finishing `terraform apply` in a single runner with `-lock-timeout=0s` to claim the lock. also will scale down orphaned ASGs once state is consistent.
sam: no objections. leave a short playbook here after recovery so we avoid this: - disable automated apply on merge for stacks that are doing state moves - add a GitLab job gate `check-consul-lock` that fails early if lock exists - make argo/helm sync avoid triggering infra apply windows
maria: adding: update docs for split-state migrations to require a 15-minute maintenance window and a brief ops channel alert.
alex: made a short checklist in the incident thread. I'll paste final actions when complete. :thumbsup:
